InputDisposition.description: What Bridge did with submitted user input. These three modes are the whole contract: a client that receives anything else is talking to a server it does not understand, so the enum is closed rather than tolerant.

oneOf.description: Nothing was running; the input started a normal turn.
A turn was running and the provider took the input natively.
A turn was running and the provider cannot take input mid-turn, so the input is durably queued for delivery at the next phase boundary.

SecretInterception.description: Mirrors `bridge_core::secret_interception::SecretInterception` — one secret replaced by a broker reference before the turn left the machine.

reference.description: The broker reference substituted into the text; the secret itself never crosses the wire.

description: `sessions/submit_input`'s result. The disposition is what the client renders; `queuedInputId` names the durable row so the optimistic message can be reconciled with its delivery, and the interceptions mirror `sessions/prepare_turn` so a steered or queued message reports replaced secrets exactly like a new turn does.
